name: Glioependymal/Ependymal Cyst

criteria.description: Identification of a well-demarcated cystic lesion lined by ependymal or glial cells on MRI or CT imaging
Histopathological confirmation showing cyst wall lined by ependymal or glial epithelium
Exclusion of other cystic lesions such as arachnoid cysts, neuroepithelial cysts, or cystic neoplasms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic cystic lesion on imaging plus histopathological confirmation with exclusion of other cyst types
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires surgical biopsy or resection for definitive confirmation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal neurological deficits correlating with cyst location
searchTerms: focal nerve deficits related to cyst

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive intracranial hypertension symptoms due to mass effect

common.symptomName: Headache associated with increased intracranial pressure
Nausea and vomiting related to raised intracranial pressure

vomiting related to increased head pressure
feeling sick due to raised intracranial pressure

common.symptomName: Visual disturbances due to optic pathway compression

visual disturbances due to optic pathway pressure

fluid buildup in brain from cyst blockage

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction due to hypothalamic or pituitary compression
searchTerms: hormone problems from pituitary or hypothalamus pressure
endocrine dysfunction due to brain compression

abnormal breathing linked to increased brain pressure

imaging: MRI showing well-circumscribed, non-enhancing cystic lesion with CSF-like intensity
CT scan revealing hypodense cystic mass without calcifications or solid components
other: Histopathology demonstrating cyst wall lined by ependymal or glial epithelium
Absence of neoplastic features in cyst lining

distinguishingFeatures: Location typically extra-axial versus intra-axial for ependymal cysts
Lack of ependymal lining on histology
Different imaging characteristics with CSF signal but no glial lining
Similar cystic appearance but lined by neuroepithelial cells distinct from ependymal cells
May have different immunohistochemical staining profiles
Often located in different CNS regions

redFlags: Rapid neurological deterioration indicating cyst expansion or hemorrhage
Signs of acute hydrocephalus such as sudden headache, vomiting, and decreased consciousness
New onset seizures or focal neurological deficits
references: Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition. IARC, 2021.
